run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: I found no sustained fault in the hotel-reservation application inside the authorized window. All 19 Deployments report 1 ready/available replica, the 21 application pods are Running with 0 restarts and no container OOM/OOMKilled/BACKOFF state, all 4 nodes report no failed conditions, all PersistentVolumeClaims are Bound, no container CPU throttling is recorded, and the sampled HTTP traffic is entirely 200: the freshest frontend sample (05:16:12) shows GET /hotels at 3382-4452 us and GET /recommendations at 1463-1637 us, and 7 sampled POST /reservation requests return 200 in 4237-8306 us; the load generator's two 30 s rounds measured p50 2.92 ms -> 3.30 ms, p90 4.84 -> 5.19 ms, p99 6.78 -> 7.30 ms (two rounds are not a baseline, so no trend is claimed). The single error-level signal in the whole namespace is one search->rate gRPC deadline: the search service's client span /rate.Rate/GetRates carries error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR with a duration of exactly 1,000,146 us at 05:14:42.891 (the very first seconds of traffic), and the corresponding rate server span took 1,048,490 us with a child mongo_rate span of 1,047,737 us. search_rate_timeouts_total and rate_requests_expired_total are both 1, with search_rate_failures_total and rate_requests_rejected_total at 0. mongodb-rate logged 8 simultaneous connection accepts plus SCRAM authentications at 05:14:42.893-42.979 from the rate pod, and mongod logged no slow-query/100 ms+ operation entries, so the ~1 s is consistent with first-use connection/authentication cost after the rate pod (started 05:14:29) and mongodb-rate (started 05:14:35) came up rather than a slow query; search's retry (max 2 attempts, 1000 ms timeout) completed in 1205 us and the user request returned HTTP 200. I considered and rejected as the active cause: revocation of the MongoDB admin readWrite role (the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps are mounted at /scripts in the two mongo pods, but rate's mongod logged createCollection rate-db.inventory at 05:14:38.348 and both geo and rate apps logged successful test-data generation at 05:14:38-39, which requires readWrite, and no post-startup localhost admin connection or authorization error appears); CPU/memory pressure (0 throttling, frontend 0.085 cores, memcached working set 4.4 MB of a 128 MB cache, mongo pods ~60 MB); and pod/node/storage failure. Two non-application observations remain open and are reported as gaps, not impact: no Ingress object exists anywhere in the cluster and the blackbox ingress probe for http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels returns probe_success=0 / probe_http_status_code=0, and the audit-log-archiver CronJob pods are reported not-ready (archiver container Completed with exit code 0, sidecar still running) which keeps KubePodNotReady firing. For the next window, re-check search_rate_timeouts_total / rate_requests_expired_total / mongo_rate latency to see whether the rate->mongodb-rate delay recurs now that the connection pool is warm; if it does, treat the rate service's MongoDB backend (mongodb-rate) as the leading suspect and check its PVC/IO latency.

Have a human retrieve the kubectl-patch that produced generation 2 of mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate at 05:14:28Z (change history / audit log, which is not available in this Run) to confirm that it only added the --auth flag and the /scripts fault-toolbox mount rather than changing anything functional.

Either deploy an ingress-nginx controller plus an Ingress for the frontend or remove the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe target so that the only currently failing monitored endpoint (probe_success=0 for http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels) reflects reality instead of a missing component.

gaps: The 24h authorized window contains only about two minutes of application telemetry: pods were created 2026-11-24T05:14:27-05:14:40, the first rate_*/search_* samples are at 05:15:13 and the trace span-metric series are effectively first sampled at 05:16:13, and Jaeger's earliest trace in my queries was 05:14:42.89. There is therefore no pre-incident baseline, no latency trend can be inferred, and any fault that began before 05:14:28 or after 05:16:13 is unobserved.

My query for pods whose status.phase is neither Running nor Succeeded across all namespaces returned no rows (the view was returned as no_data, so it is not citable as proof of absence); I cannot claim from it that no pod was unhealthy earlier in the window.

The cause of the load generator's 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 188' line, which appears with the identical value 188 in both round #0 and round #1, is unresolved: its recorded latency distribution tops out at 11.44 ms (round #0) and 10.2 ms (round #1) and its HdrHistogram total count (1947) does not match its reported request count (2971), while node TCP counters (TCPTimeouts, TCPSynRetrans, ListenOverflows, ListenDrops) did not increase during 05:15:13-05:16:13. I cannot attribute those timeouts to a specific service.

Jaeger/span-metric coverage is partial: the frontend recorded ~3,280 HTTP server spans in a period in which the load generator reported ~5,905 requests, and the spans are exported over Jaeger UDP (lossy), so per-operation error rates and the completeness of the call graph are unknown; the projected span samples are biased, not a failure rate.

The rate service's mongo_rate spans carry no status tag (status_state not_recorded), so whether each individual rate->mongodb-rate read succeeded cannot be confirmed from traces; mongod does not log command-level authorization results either.

No Ingress object exists in the cluster and no ingress-nginx controller namespace is present, so the application's external /api/hotels path could not be exercised; only the failing blackbox probe result is available for it.

The change_history integration is not configured in this Run, so the content of the kubectl-patch at 05:14:28Z that created generation 2 of mongodb-geo / mongodb-rate is unknown; only its side effects (new ReplicaSets, old ones scaled to 0, unchanged mongo:4.4.6 image and --auth args, plus the newly visible /scripts failure-script mount) are visible.

I could not verify any MongoDB data content or role membership directly (no database tool is registered and Secrets cannot be read); statements about admin privileges rest on log evidence from mongod and the applications.

The audit-log-archiver pods' not-ready state produced a firing KubePodNotReady alert; I read the archiver container's Completed/exit 0 status and its CronJob but did not read those pods' application logs, so this remains an unexplained-but-benign-looking side finding rather than a cleared one.
next_steps: Re-query search_rate_timeouts_total, rate_requests_expired_total and mongo_rate latency over a later window (now that the rate connection pool is warm) to distinguish a one-off cold-start delay from a persistent rate->mongodb-rate latency fault.
Retrieve the kubectl-patch/audit-log entry for mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate at 2026-11-24T05:14:28Z from change history, which is not integrated here.

If the sregym-style fault toolbox is expected to be exercised in this scenario, record explicitly whether revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh / revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh are intended to be executed, since the ConfigMaps are mounted but no execution evidence exists.
Deploy an Ingress/ingress-nginx or retire the blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation probe target so the ingress probe stops failing on a missing component.

Investigate the load generator's socket-timeout accounting (identical 188 per 30 s round) with its job spec and wrk2 Lua script, which were not present in the hotel-reservation namespace during this Run.
